# Modular distinct subset sums

[All problems](../README.md) · [Lab](../../README.md) · [Progress](../../PROGRESS.md) · [Contribute](../../CONTRIBUTING.md)

**Project focus: PARKED.** Understand the structure of n-element sets with all subset sums distinct modulo 2^n+5.

## The question

Compare admissible sets with signed unit dilations of {1,2,4,...,2^(n-1)}. This is a separately tracked research branch; no unverified Erdős problem number is assigned.

## Read this first

The certified n=6 result is not a proof for every n. Sign reduction, completeness and the independent checker are part of the finite claim.

### Modulus 69: complete n=6 case

4,224 admissible sets; each is within one replacement of signed unit-scaled powers of two. No all-n theorem.

Formalization: **UNFORMALIZED**. Literature: **PRIORITY_UNCHECKED**.

## Next bounded question

At n=7 and modulus 133, can an admissible set require more than one replacement to reach a signed, unit-scaled powers-of-two set?

**Discriminating test:** One fully verified set at replacement distance at least two refutes the proposed all-n pattern. An incomplete search with no counterexample does not prove it.
